summary: US stocks split: the Dow topped 50,000 while the Nasdaq fell 1.5% as Nvidia and chip stocks gave back Monday's surge; gold slid 2.7% on Fed hike bets and the 10y held near 4.90% ahead of PCE.

ES.why: S&P fell 0.5% as chips sold off while the Dow rose; funds are crowded long (94th pct), PCE in 15h.
ES.risk: Soft PCE and chip rebound would tilt bullish; hot PCE bearish.

NQ.why: Nasdaq -1.5% as Nvidia gave back ~7% of Monday's 31% jump and AMD/Micron slid; funds lean long (85th pct).
NQ.risk: Hot PCE extends the chip selloff; soft PCE revives the AI bid.

YM.why: Dow rose 0.85% to a record above 50,000 on rotation out of tech, but Fed hike bets and PCE make it unproven.
YM.risk: A second day of rotation after a soft PCE would tilt bullish.

RTY.why: Russell 2000 +0.6% on rotation and strong consumer confidence, but small caps are most exposed to a Fed hike.
RTY.risk: Hot PCE hits rate-sensitive small caps hardest.

NKD.why: Nikkei down ~10% over 20 days and US chip selloff weighs, but positioning is neutral (32nd pct) and PCE is close.
NKD.risk: Chip rebound plus soft PCE would lift it; deeper chip losses sink it.

6E.why: EUR/USD near 1.09 under pressure from French budget worries and ~95% odds of a Dec Fed hike; PCE decides next leg.
6E.risk: Soft PCE lifts the euro; hot PCE extends dollar strength.

6J.why: USD/JPY near 159 with Katayama warning on rapid moves and a December BoJ hike expected; PCE could swing it.
6J.risk: Intervention or a hot PCE spike in USD/JPY are the two-way risks.

6B.why: No fresh UK driver found overnight; pound trades off the dollar ahead of US PCE.
6B.risk: A US PCE surprise sets the direction.

6A.why: No fresh Australian driver found; chip selloff is a risk-off drag but PCE is the bigger swing.
6A.risk: Risk-on after soft PCE would lift AUD.

ZN.why: 10y yield 4.90%, little changed, with a Dec Fed hike ~95% priced; PCE is the next test.
ZN.risk: Hot PCE pushes yields up (ZN down); soft PCE rallies bonds.

GC.why: Gold fell 2.7% to ~$3,552 on hawkish Fed bets; funds lean short (20th pct), which cushions further downside.
GC.risk: A soft PCE could spark a short squeeze higher.

CL.why: Crude held near $81-83 with Gulf shipping attacks vs supply worries; funds crowded short (10th pct), OPEC+ meets 29 Nov.
CL.risk: A Hormuz supply hit squeezes shorts higher; a US-Iran deal sinks it.
